rows.narration: Imagine Japan around seventeen twenty. You belong to a samurai household, wear two swords, and hold a rank that most people can never claim.
rows.action: Wide same-master view: Kenji stands at the gate threshold, upright and composed, both sheathed swords at anatomical left hip, hands relaxed, cream round head clearly visible. Gate and bench remain unobstructed.

rows.narration: From a distance, this looks like an excellent arrangement. You have status, a family name, and a very dramatic way to enter a room.
rows.action: Medium same-angle view: Kenji enters the gate with a restrained confident expression, one small hand lightly touching his obi, both sheaths still worn. No combat or weapon drawn.

rows.narration: Then you look at the family accounts. Your sword is valuable. Your reputation is valuable. Unfortunately, the rice merchant wants money instead of either.
rows.action: Kenji and Hana sit beside the existing low desk, looking at the open household ledger and a few bronze coins. His eyebrows fall as Hana points calmly at the accounts; the ledger stays on the desk.

rows.narration: You are a retainer near the lower end of the ladder. The country has enjoyed decades of relative peace, but your obligations have not retired.
rows.action: Senior stands behind the existing desk handing Kenji a closed cream paper order tied by brown cord. Kenji accepts it with both hands; the one register, brush holder and inkstone remain fixed.

rows.narration: Your problem is not simply surviving a duel. It is surviving a system that expects you to look respectable, obey your superiors, and fund the performance.
rows.action: Kenji holds the closed order at chest height while Senior points toward the guard bench. Both have the same duty clothing and sheathed weapons; show responsibility through posture, not a sword fight.

rows.narration: The famous picture gives you a fearless warrior beneath the cherry blossoms. The ordinary picture adds a leaking roof, paperwork, and somebody asking about payment.
rows.action: Hana holds one folded indigo garment by the existing shelf while Kenji compares a small repair cloth and household ledger. Show ordinary expenses in the fixed room; no rain, roof destruction or new window.

rows.narration: This is the contradiction at the center of your life. You belong to a privileged military class, but privilege does not make you wealthy or independent.
rows.action: At the fixed left counter, the merchant presents a plain wooden rice measure while Kenji offers a few bronze coins. Merchant is composed, Kenji anxious; all sacks, noren and handcart stay in place.

rows.narration: Your swords tell everyone who you are. They do not tell anyone whether your household can afford another bad month, another journey, or another obligation.
rows.action: Kenji opens an almost-empty small cloth coin pouch beside the household ledger as Hana looks on thoughtfully. No text or numeric balance; the desk, shelf and doorway stay exactly in the master geometry.

rows.narration: So keep the swords. You will need the identity they represent. Just understand that the hardest battle may begin when you sit down with a ledger.
rows.action: Kenji sets the closed pouch beside the ledger, then looks toward his still-worn swords with a small resigned expression. Clear paper-versus-weapon contrast without extra blades, written text or invented props. Any coin pouch visible is ONE small plain BROWN cloth pouch, not blue/mauve/patterned.

rows.narration: Long before you receive your first assignment, your family has an assignment for you. Continue the household, preserve its position, and avoid becoming its disaster.
rows.action: Father sits beside the existing desk giving adult Kenji a stern but calm household instruction, pointing to a plain bound family register. Kenji listens with both hands on his knees.

rows.narration: Your name is more than a personal label. It connects you to a lineage, a lord, and expectations that existed before you were able to understand them.
rows.action: Father and Mother flank adult Kenji beside the low desk, examining a cream lineage scroll with indistinct brush marks. Show belonging and inherited expectations; no child version or extra unnamed family members.

rows.narration: The samurai order is not a single, equal club. An influential official and a poorly paid retainer can share a status while living very different lives.
rows.action: Senior sits at the fixed desk reviewing a register while Kenji stands patiently at a respectful distance. Same cream faces and simple garments; body placement conveys rank without adding a throne or raised dais.

rows.narration: Birth gives some households a considerable advantage. Family connections, hereditary standing, and the particular rules of your domain help shape what opportunities you can reach.
rows.action: Senior selects one paper from a modest stack and indicates a task to Kenji, who waits empty-handed beside the desk. Paper cubbies and window remain unchanged; no extra officer or costume swap.

rows.narration: Ability can still matter. Education, useful skills, and a superior's favor may improve your prospects. But being talented does not make the hierarchy disappear.
rows.action: Senior holds a small plain learning scroll while Kenji reads attentively before practice, both standing near the open left veranda. Wood training weapons stay on the rear-right wall; no chalkboard or text labels.

rows.narration: Your father teaches you how to behave before important men. Your mother understands which household decisions will become everybody's problem if they are handled badly.
rows.action: Father demonstrates a restrained respectful bow to adult Kenji while Mother observes with folded hands. Keep the family grouping beside the desk and doorway open; no extravagant kneeling procession or costume change.

rows.narration: If your household needs an heir, adoption may offer a solution. Family continuity is important enough that blood and household membership do not always follow identical paths.
rows.action: All three adults review a plain household document together; Mother places a careful hand on the paper while Father addresses Kenji. Illustrate continuity and succession with records, not babies or unexplained new heirs.

rows.narration: That does not turn your life into a free choice of careers. Leaving the obligations attached to your household can carry consequences for people beyond yourself.
rows.action: Kenji stands between Father and Senior at the fixed gate, holding the household document close to his chest. The elder men face him with serious calm expressions; no departure in changed weather.

rows.narration: You inherit advantages that a farmer or servant lacks. You also inherit a role whose instruction manual seems to have been written without consulting you.
rows.action: Kenji sits between the two elders, looking from the lineage scroll on the desk to their expectant faces. Use the same scroll/room and grown character identities to convey inherited role and limited choice.

rows.narration: Now comes the unexpected part. You are a member of a military class in a society where many samurai spend their working lives doing something else.
rows.action: Kenji writes carefully in the existing bound register while Senior checks a separate loose paper at the desk edge. A warrior doing ordinary work; both sheathed pairs remain worn and no paper becomes a weapon.

rows.narration: The Tokugawa order has brought relative stability after an earlier age of civil war. The great battles in family stories are not your ordinary morning appointment.
rows.action: Senior points at the two mounted wooden practice weapons while Kenji listens with a reflective expression. Empty practice floor and ordinary daylight suggest peacetime; no inserted battlefield, ancestral portrait or armor.

rows.narration: Domains still need guards and trained men. They also need officials, messengers, inspectors, teachers, and people capable of managing an impressive quantity of written business.
rows.action: Kenji carries a small stack of plain registers toward Senior, who gestures to an available part of the existing desk. Show clerical/messenger work through useful objects, not invented readable job-title signs.

rows.narration: Your assignment might involve watching an entrance, carrying an order, checking a register, or assisting an office. None of these duties comes with a heroic soundtrack.
rows.action: Kenji checks a small paper register at the fixed gate opening, looking up attentively toward an unseen arriving visitor. One role, one document; bench and storage cabinet unchanged, no new guard silhouette.

rows.narration: Literacy becomes a practical advantage. You may study writing and classical learning alongside martial skills, depending on your household, resources, and opportunities.
rows.action: Father sits at the desk showing Kenji how to hold a brush above a plain learning paper. The existing inkstone and brush holder remain on the desk; illegible ink marks only, same adult Kenji.

rows.narration: The military identity remains important even when the work looks administrative. You cannot simply announce that peace has arrived and military expectations should therefore be optional.
rows.action: Both adults perform a restrained introductory bow before practice, hands empty, two mounted wooden weapons still behind them. Their real sheathed swords stay at anatomical left hips; no sudden metal duel.

rows.narration: Weapons, discipline, and readiness still belong to your role. So do the less glamorous habits that keep an office, a gate, or a household functioning.
rows.action: Senior inspects Kenji's tidy duty clothing and sheathed sword fittings while Kenji stands still. No drawn blade; fixed warm daylight, gate geometry and covered bench remain identical to earlier duty shots.

rows.narration: You may admire an ancestor's battlefield exploits. Today you are trying to impress a superior by delivering the correct information to the correct person.
rows.action: Kenji presents the closed tied order to Senior with both hands while Senior reaches to receive it at the desk. Show correct delivery to the correct person, not a heroic battle pose.

rows.narration: The sword is still at your side. It just spends a surprising amount of time accompanying you to meetings that could have been a shorter letter.
rows.action: Kenji and Senior study the same open register from opposite sides of the existing low desk, quietly serious. Keep the room camera orientation, windows, cubbies and paper arrangement stable.

rows.narration: Looking like a samurai requires objects, and objects require upkeep. Clothing wears out. Equipment needs attention. A household needs repairs whether its name is distinguished or not.
rows.action: Hana examines a worn sleeve on a folded indigo garment while Kenji notices the limited coins beside the ledger. His current worn kosode stays intact and identical; the repair garment is a separate folded object.

rows.narration: Your position may bring expectations about suitable dress and conduct. Showing up poorly prepared can make a private money problem look like a public failure.
rows.action: Senior quietly adjusts the position of a small duty document in Kenji's hands, preparing him for service. Kenji stands neat and attentive; illustrate presentability without new insignia, banners or formal clothing.

rows.narration: A sword needs proper care. A damaged fitting or neglected blade will not repair itself simply because your family has several stories about courage.
rows.action: Kenji seated beside the fixed low desk wipes the fitting of ONE of his TWO STILL-WORN SHEATHED swords with a small plain cloth. BOTH black scabbards remain at his anatomical-left hip. No sword held loose, no blade drawn, no empty sheath on desk, no third weapon. Same HOME geometry and duty costume.
rows.visual_action_origin: root-regeneration clarification to avoid original duplicate-weapon failure
rows.original_action_before_regeneration: Kenji seated near the low desk carefully wipes an exposed short section of ONE sword with a plain cloth; its own black empty sheath rests on the desk, SECOND sword remains sheathed at left hip. Exactly two swords total, no duplicates.

rows.narration: You also need clothing for the tasks expected of you. A formal occasion, ordinary service, and travel do not necessarily demand the same preparations.
rows.action: Hana places a neatly folded dark garment beside the left shelf while Kenji compares it with his current indigo sleeve. Show preparation for an occasion; do not change Kenji's worn outfit or add armor.

rows.narration: Your wife examines a garment and considers repairing it again. You consider whether anyone important will notice. These are different versions of the same financial discussion.
rows.action: Hana lifts the folded garment and traces a worn seam with one small black hand while Kenji looks cautiously toward the doorway. Same repair object, same shelf and unchanged household outfit identities.

rows.narration: Even a useful purchase competes with another useful purchase. Replace the worn footwear, attend to the roof, or keep enough cash available for an unexpected obligation.
rows.action: At the desk, Kenji holds a worn plain straw sandal while Hana points toward the accounts and a small repair cloth. Three competing household expenses shown physically, no floating icons or written numbers.

rows.narration: Displays of luxury can be regulated, and customs vary between domains and ranks. This is not a world where every samurai simply dresses however he wishes.
rows.action: Merchant presents a modest plain fabric roll across the fixed counter; Kenji considers it without buying. Keep rice stock and sacks behind the merchant unchanged; no modern luxurious cloth print or shop redesign.

rows.narration: Your armor is not an everyday costume for visiting a rice seller. The household can own military equipment without spending every ordinary afternoon dressed for battle.
rows.action: Kenji checks a modest closed wooden equipment box beside the desk while Hana tidies the folded garment at the shelf. No armor worn, no battle props scattered, nothing in the room moves without the action.

rows.narration: The romantic image gives you the complete outfit for free. Your actual household has to acquire it, maintain it, store it, and argue about its cost.
rows.action: Hana holds the closed cloth pouch as Kenji places the repaired sandal beside the desk, both slightly weary but cooperative. Existing ledger, garment and equipment box form a quiet practical household scene. Any coin pouch visible is ONE small plain BROWN cloth pouch, not blue/mauve/patterned.

rows.narration: Many samurai incomes were connected to stipends measured in rice, although payment arrangements varied. A figure written in grain does not automatically mean bags arrive unchanged.
rows.action: Merchant weighs a small amount of rice using a modest portable balance placed on the existing counter while Kenji watches. Rice measures/sacks remain fixed; show payment arrangements without legible numbers.

rows.narration: Even when rice is involved, your household needs things that are bought with money. Clothing, repairs, travel expenses, and numerous purchases complicate the arithmetic.
rows.action: Hana lays a plain repair cloth and straw sandal beside the ledger as Kenji opens the coin pouch. No magical full purse or costume changes; ordinary purchases physically surround the accounts.

rows.narration: Converting grain into cash links your income to prices and intermediaries. The value written beside your rank and the money available in your hand are different questions.
rows.action: Merchant hands Kenji a small tied coin pouch across the counter beside one plain rice measure. Show grain-to-cash exchange, with both actors' hands contacting the same single pouch.

rows.narration: A merchant examines the transaction calmly. You examine it as a man who would prefer the numbers to become more respectful of his social standing.
rows.action: Merchant points at a plain open ledger on the counter while Kenji studies the coin pouch in his hand with raised worried brows. Same transaction setting, no unreadable giant writing or money signs.

rows.narration: Social rank does not force market prices to behave. If your available income buys less than before, the family budget experiences that change very personally.
rows.action: Kenji pours only a few bronze coins from the pouch onto the desk beside the unchanged ledger. Hana measures a small rice portion in a wooden bowl; no exaggerated starvation or displayed price figures.

rows.narration: Debt became a serious problem for many samurai households and domains. Borrowing can bridge an immediate gap while making a later gap considerably less pleasant.
rows.action: Kenji bends slightly toward the merchant requesting help, hands holding a closed paper pledge; merchant studies it calmly. The ledger stays on the same counter and no official status suddenly changes either outfit.

rows.narration: The lender belongs to a socially different position, yet controls something you currently need. Economic power and official status are not always carried by the same person.
rows.action: Merchant keeps one hand on the counter ledger and another on the small coin pouch while Kenji waits anxiously. Visualize economic leverage through expressions and objects, no villain costume or threatening weapon.

rows.narration: Your household may seek extra income where circumstances and local rules permit. Teaching, skilled work, or other activities could matter more than the glamorous image suggests.
rows.action: Kenji teaches from a small open learning scroll at the desk, pointing gently with an empty hand toward an unseen adult pupil off camera. No new child actor, classroom furniture or written labels.

rows.narration: At the end of the conversation, your swords remain sharp. The lender's accounting brush is also in excellent condition, and today its performance matters much more.
rows.action: Merchant closes his ledger deliberately while Kenji holds the modest tied coin pouch beside his still-sheathed pair. Clear brush/accounting versus warrior status contrast; no sword drawn or intimidation.

rows.narration: The relationship with your lord gives your position its meaning. You are not simply an independent swordsman wandering wherever the next picturesque landscape happens to appear.
rows.action: Senior waits at the fixed gate with a closed order while Kenji approaches attentively. The gate identifies ordinary structured service, not an independent adventurer posing in a new landscape.

rows.narration: Service brings duties, supervision, and a place within a chain of authority. Your immediate superior may be the person whose decisions shape most of your working day.
rows.action: Senior stands at the desk checking a paper register as Kenji waits with hands lowered. Their spacing and calm restrained faces indicate supervision; keep two named actors and no random extra magistrate.

rows.narration: An order arrives while you are dealing with another problem. You do not get to decline because your household has decided this week is already inconvenient.
rows.action: Senior delivers a closed tied paper order at the existing open rear-right doorway while Kenji turns from the ledger to receive it and Hana pauses garment repair. Fixed room, same daylight and no door relocation.

rows.narration: There may be guard duty, an inspection, an errand, or office work. The exact arrangements depend on the domain, your rank, and the particular job you hold.
rows.action: Kenji stands alert beside the unchanged covered bench, holding a small gate register and looking toward the entry. A specific guard assignment, no dramatic armor, hidden weapons or inconsistent outfit.

rows.narration: Some assignments involve responsibility without much freedom. You are accountable for an outcome while relying on people and decisions that you do not entirely control.
rows.action: Kenji points to a small pile of pending records while Senior indicates another closed document. Show responsibility with incomplete control; all papers remain grounded on the existing desk.

rows.narration: A misplaced item needs an explanation. A delayed message needs an explanation. A superior's request for an explanation can become a substantial part of the afternoon.
rows.action: Kenji opens an otherwise empty plain paper folder as Senior raises one questioning eyebrow. Show a misplaced document problem without comic text, extra limbs or missing architecture.

rows.narration: Rank also shapes whose inconvenience matters most. An influential man's delay may become everybody else's emergency, including yours, even when your own task was carefully planned.
rows.action: Senior gives Kenji another tied order while the first paper folder and open register remain on the desk. Kenji looks at the growing task pile, not a different face or suddenly changed room.

rows.narration: Serving effectively can bring pride and a secure sense of belonging. That benefit is real, which makes losing the position more frightening rather than less.
rows.action: Kenji returns to the desk and sits beside Hana, placing a sealed order carefully away from the household ledger. The service document and personal accounts are distinct physical objects.

rows.narration: The system gives you an identity, an income, and obligations. They arrive together. There is no convenient option to keep the first two and cancel the third.
rows.action: Senior hands Kenji the regular closed order at the gate; Kenji receives it respectfully with both hands, clearly belonging to the organization. Same duty setting and fixed sheathed sword count.

rows.narration: Peace does not remove the need to train. Martial skills remain connected to your status, even when your most frequent opponent is an administrative deadline.
rows.action: Kenji and Senior hold ONE plain wooden practice weapon each in calm ready stance on the clear floor. Wall mounts are EMPTY because the two wooden weapons have been taken down; real sword pairs remain sheathed. EXACT prop inventory: TWO wooden practice rods total, ONE held by EACH man, EMPTY wall brackets. Both men ALSO retain exactly TWO SHEATHED STEEL swords each at anatomical LEFT hips; never add a third held steel weapon.

rows.narration: Instruction differs between schools, families, and opportunities. There is no single standardized program that produces every samurai in exactly the same manner.
rows.action: Same practice session: Senior demonstrates a simple controlled grip while Kenji watches, each still holding the same single wooden weapon. Rear wall weapon mounts remain empty; no duplicate wooden blades. EXACT prop inventory: TWO wooden practice rods total, ONE held by EACH man, EMPTY wall brackets. Both men ALSO retain exactly TWO SHEATHED STEEL swords each at anatomical LEFT hips; never add a third held steel weapon.

rows.narration: You practice controlled movement with a wooden training weapon. Repetition is less exciting to watch than a duel, but considerably more relevant to learning a skill.
rows.action: Kenji repeats a basic controlled wooden-weapon movement as Senior supervises from a safe distance. Same prop counts and empty mounts, no contact fight, speed streaks, drawn metal swords or altered costume. EXACT prop inventory: TWO wooden practice rods total, ONE held by EACH man, EMPTY wall brackets. Both men ALSO retain exactly TWO SHEATHED STEEL swords each at anatomical LEFT hips; never add a third held steel weapon.

rows.narration: An instructor corrects your posture. Again. Your family name has apparently failed to persuade your shoulders to occupy the correct position without assistance.
rows.action: Senior points with a free hand at Kenji's elbow position; Kenji holds the wooden practice weapon steady and looks mildly embarrassed. Preserve wall/door/floor, no anatomical flesh hands or extra arms. EXACT prop inventory: TWO wooden practice rods total, ONE held by EACH man, EMPTY wall brackets. Both men ALSO retain exactly TWO SHEATHED STEEL swords each at anatomical LEFT hips; never add a third held steel weapon.

rows.narration: Fiction makes drawing a sword look like a useful response to every disagreement. In an organized society, violence can create legal and political problems extremely quickly.
rows.action: Back on ordinary duty, Senior speaks calmly to Kenji while Kenji keeps both hands well away from his sheathed sword hilts. Practice weapons are absent in this new gate scene, no sudden combat.

rows.narration: An ordinary insult does not give every samurai unlimited permission to kill. Laws, investigation, context, and the involvement of authorities make the real situation more complicated.
rows.action: Kenji sits before Senior at the fixed desk, listening to a serious explanation over a paper record. Suggest investigation and rules through official papers, no execution imagery, punishments or gore.

rows.narration: You may possess privileges that others lack, but your lord still has an interest in preventing disorder. Your personal outrage is not the only consideration.
rows.action: Senior lowers one hand in a calming gesture while Kenji breathes and relaxes his posture beside the gate. Both keep exactly their sheathed pairs and neither draws a blade.

rows.narration: A disciplined retainer can resolve a tense encounter without turning the street into a battlefield. Restraint does not make the consequences of the encounter less serious.
rows.action: Kenji and Merchant resolve a tense discussion calmly across the fixed rice counter, Kenji's hands open, merchant pointing to ledger. No brandishing sword, threatening pose or new bystander.

rows.narration: You return home after practice with tired arms and another obligation completed. Nobody has produced a legendary victory, but the day has remained usefully free of catastrophe.
rows.action: Kenji rests seated with tired shoulders while Hana offers a small plain cup beside the desk. His sword pair is still sheathed; the scene is quiet recovery, not injury or melodramatic victory.

rows.narration: Your household is not a quiet background to your individual adventure. It is where rank, income, marriage, inheritance, and daily practical work all meet.
rows.action: Kenji and Hana review household items together at the desk: ledger, plain cup, folded repair garment and tied pouch, all placed coherently. They cooperate rather than perform a warrior adventure. Any coin pouch visible is ONE small plain BROWN cloth pouch, not blue/mauve/patterned.

rows.narration: Marriage can involve family strategies, status, and the continuation of the household. Personal affection may exist, but it is not the only force shaping the arrangement.
rows.action: Four named adults discuss a household document around the existing low desk, Hana and Kenji side by side, the older parents across. No wedding stage, new costume, random child or real historical person.

rows.narration: Your wife manages practical concerns that do not disappear while you serve elsewhere. Food, clothing, finances, relatives, and household relationships all require attention.
rows.action: Hana alone sorts the ledger, repairs a seam on the separate folded garment and looks toward the shelf, illustrating daily management. All fixed furniture remains, no added bed/kitchen/cupboard.

rows.narration: Women's experiences vary considerably with resources, rank, place, and circumstance. Treating every samurai wife as either powerless or secretly commanding an army misses that variation.
rows.action: Mother advises Hana beside the desk, both calmly comparing the family register and folded clothing. Preserve their distinct blue-gray versus mauve robes and low bun identities.

rows.narration: She can understand the household's financial danger before you finish giving it a more dignified name. An obligation sounds less impressive when somebody must pay for it.
rows.action: Hana points directly at the few coins beside the open ledger while Kenji holds a service order and considers its cost. One clear household reality versus duty exchange, no written labels or cartoon speech bubbles.

rows.narration: Children and dependents add responsibilities, while illness or an unexpected loss can disturb a careful plan. A distinguished family still has to manage ordinary human vulnerability.
rows.action: Mother sits quietly with a plain cup while Hana attends to her and Kenji checks the household accounts. Illustrate dependency/care without adding children, medical machines or exaggerated sickness.

rows.narration: Education, marriage prospects, and succession can become long projects. Decisions are made with the future of the household in mind, sometimes at the expense of individual wishes.
rows.action: Father hands Kenji a plain family register while Hana examines a small learning scroll beside it. Show long-term family decisions through existing papers, no new furniture or inherited costume change.

rows.narration: Family continuity may involve an adopted heir, an advantageous marriage, or support from connections. The available choices are shaped by rules as well as personal preference.
rows.action: All four adults consider a household record together, Mother presenting it to Kenji. Adult adoption/continuity is conveyed by family deliberation; no literal signature text, baby or newly invented relative.

rows.narration: Your household's reputation is shared. A reckless choice can reach people who were nowhere near the incident and who have to live with its consequences afterward.
rows.action: Kenji gently sets the closed service order beside the household register while Hana looks concerned; both understand shared consequences. Same room, objects remain in deliberate positions, no time-of-day flip.

rows.narration: One major obligation connects the domains to the shogunate. Alternate attendance requires many lords to spend periods in Edo, with important exceptions and changing arrangements.
rows.action: Kenji and Senior stand on the master road near the inn, a single BROWN cloth travel bundle grounded at Kenji's feet. Each carries a closed order, showing assigned journey; no lord portrait or giant procession crowd.

rows.narration: It is the lord's obligation, not a rule that every individual samurai follows in an identical personal rotation. But retainers can be drawn into its practical demands.
rows.action: Explicit explanatory cut back to planning: Senior indicates a plain route scroll to Kenji at the fixed domain desk. Use the same office, not a map with invented labels or a uniform everybody-following line.

rows.narration: If you are assigned to the traveling party, the procession becomes a moving workplace. There are belongings, arrangements, responsibilities, and plenty of people to keep coordinated.
rows.action: Return to the same road: Kenji now carries the single brown cloth bundle by its tied handle, Senior checking the closed order beside him. Bridge/inn/slopes fixed, weather unchanged, no second bundle on ground.

rows.narration: The magnificent public appearance hides preparation and expense. Roads, lodgings, clothing, baggage, and attendants all participate in a system that looks better from outside the accounts.
rows.action: At the master inn entrance on left, Kenji examines a small coin pouch while Senior checks their closed travel order. The ONE brown cloth bundle is grounded beside Kenji's feet. Show preparation expenses without inventing an innkeeper or moving the market merchant here.

rows.narration: The political purpose is larger than your comfort. The system helps bind lords to the Tokugawa order and imposes significant obligations on their resources and households.
rows.action: Senior studies the route scroll and a small travel account record at the fixed desk, alone. This is an explanatory administrative insert, not a claim that all individual retainers alternate personally.

rows.narration: Lords' wives and heirs residing in Edo are part of that structure. This does not mean every lower-ranking retainer's wife is automatically held there under the same arrangement.
rows.action: Hana and Mother manage their own household ledger beside the same desk during Kenji's absence. Show lower-retainer family at HOME, not in a prison, hostage palace or distant Edo room.

rows.narration: While you are away, your own household still needs to function. The roof, accounts, and family problems have not received official permission to wait for your return.
rows.action: Hana tends the folded repair garment and checks the same open ledger while Kenji is absent. The home remains bright and structurally intact, no weather jump or new unattended fire.

rows.narration: In Edo, retainer life may involve service at a domain residence rather than sightseeing. The capital is impressive, but your employer has not sent you on holiday.
rows.action: Kenji arrives beside Senior in the different Edo service room, places the ONE brown travel bundle at the master's near-right floor position, and reaches toward the desk register. Distinct windows/shelf geometry maintained.

rows.narration: You wanted a position with dignity and belonging. It has also given you a journey whose impressive number of moving parts includes your already uncomfortable budget.
rows.action: Kenji sits at the low service desk writing in the register while Senior holds a new closed duty order. Brown bundle stays at near-right floor; no sightseeing skyline, new costume, swords removed or room redesigned. EXACTLY ONE brown cloth travel bundle remains on NEAR-RIGHT FLOOR, fully grounded; not on desk or left floor.

rows.narration: The fear behind all these obligations is the possibility of losing your place. A family dependent on service has good reason to care about its continuation.
rows.action: Explanatory return to household concerns: Kenji and Hana consider a closed order beside the personal ledger, brows worried. No literal time elapsed/age change; use same adult identities and exact home geometry.

rows.narration: If a lord loses his domain, a household is dissolved, or employment ends, a retainer's future can change dramatically. The circumstances are not identical in every case.
rows.action: Senior presents an unfamiliar closed official notice while Kenji listens with a serious face. Suggest employment uncertainty through document and reaction, not burning castle, severed head or actual domain identified by text.

rows.narration: A masterless samurai is often described as a ronin. The word does not automatically identify a romantic wanderer who spends every afternoon winning another impossible duel.
rows.action: Kenji stands alone just outside the same gate holding the notice close to his chest, contemplating loss of position. Keep his sheathed pair and costume unchanged, no ragged ronin outfit or changed season.

rows.narration: It may identify someone seeking work, relying on connections, teaching a skill, or facing uncertainty. Losing an established position can be a material problem as well as an emotional one.
rows.action: Kenji cautiously asks Merchant about work while holding a small learning scroll, merchant listens across the fixed counter. No wandering assassin, drawn sword, bandit prop or instant employer handshake.

rows.narration: Your social identity may outlast the income attached to it. That creates an uncomfortable situation when you still have a household to support and expectations to maintain.
rows.action: Hana shows the nearly empty cloth pouch to Kenji beside the family ledger; his sheathed swords and rank costume remain. Illustrate identity surviving lost income, not sudden clothing or hairstyle deterioration.

rows.narration: Finding another employer can depend on reputation, skills, opportunities, and introductions. A dramatic declaration of independence is not a guaranteed replacement for regular support.
rows.action: Kenji offers a plain folded letter of introduction to Senior, who considers it at the same desk. Show the importance of connections and skill, not a guaranteed promotion or new rank insignia.

rows.narration: Even while employed, a retainer can worry about dismissal, disgrace, or political change beyond his control. Keeping the position becomes a form of everyday risk management.
rows.action: Kenji pauses beside the gate bench studying the folded letter with lowered worried brows. Intact gate and unchanged duty appearance keep uncertainty grounded; no chained prisoner or violent threat.

rows.narration: You might resent the restrictions of service and still fear the alternative. Dependence can be frustrating, particularly when losing it does not immediately create a better option.
rows.action: Kenji and Hana sit at the fixed low desk, quietly looking at ONE folded cream duty letter and the same small BROWN cloth coin pouch. Concerned brows, composed posture, two sword hilts at Kenji's anatomical-left hip if visible. Keep modest house geometry and ledger; no prisoner, armor or lavish room.

rows.narration: So you check the document once more, maintain the equipment, and avoid an unnecessary quarrel. These small decisions are connected to a much larger question: can your household continue?
rows.action: Kenji reads the ONE folded cream document in his left hand while the other holds a small plain cloth against the fitting of ONE of his TWO STILL-WORN sheathed swords. Both black scabbards remain at anatomical-left hip; no loose blade, third sword or extra sheath. The ledger stays at the fixed desk.

rows.narration: Later stories often present the samurai as followers of one eternal, uniform code. Historical conduct and ideas were more varied than that polished image suggests.
rows.action: Senior reads ONE plain open bound register at the existing low office desk, thoughtfully, illustrating historical ideas rather than a magical universal code. Two sheathed swords at anatomical-left hip. Preserve shoji, cubbies, cushions and desk props; no visible labels, modern book cover or floating symbols.

rows.narration: Different periods, writers, schools, and households emphasized different ideals. Loyalty, duty, discipline, courage, and learning could matter without producing identical choices in every situation.
rows.action: Kenji and Senior calmly compare TWO separate plain paper documents laid side by side on the fixed office desk, one pointing at each document. Same identity costumes and office orientation, no readable text or ideal-code overlays; exactly two worn swords per man.

rows.narration: A man in seventeen twenty is not simply acting out the modern version of bushido. Later interpretations can turn a changing history into an apparently timeless rulebook.
rows.action: Kenji studies ONE thin plain bound record, held open over the existing low desk, with a thoughtful expression. The other register remains on desk, not duplicated in his hands. No modern bushido title, sacred glowing text or fantasy armor; fixed everyday office scene.

rows.narration: In practice, obligations may collide. What helps your family can conflict with what a superior wants. What preserves a reputation can create a financial or personal cost.
rows.action: Hana points to the modest household ledger and small BROWN coin pouch on the desk while Kenji holds ONE folded cream duty order beside it, visibly weighing the competing obligations. Same HOME geography, quiet restrained expressions, no extra letters/pouch or costume changes.

rows.narration: There is rarely a useful voice announcing the morally perfect answer. You have other people's expectations, incomplete information, and consequences that will remain after the decision.
rows.action: Kenji stands beside the fixed covered bench, studying ONE folded cream paper order and considering his next step, one empty hand resting at his obi. Unchanged gate, cabinet, pine and daylight. Both black sword scabbards stay worn on anatomical-left hip; no magic voice, violence or thought-bubble text.

rows.narration: Seppuku also belongs to this history, but it is not the automatic response to every error or embarrassment. Context, authority, punishment, and exceptional circumstances matter.
rows.action: Senior calmly places ONE closed cream formal letter on the existing low office desk, beside the ordinary register, showing administrative authority and context. Both swords remain SHEATHED and WORN; empty other hand, no death scene, blade drawn, prisoner or bloody imagery.

rows.narration: The ordinary mistake in an office does not instantly become a mandatory death sentence. Making every setback end that way misunderstands both administration and human survival.
rows.action: Senior points to ONE erroneous entry represented by tiny indistinct marks in the open register while Kenji corrects it with the existing writing brush. Ordinary restrained office correction, not punishment scene. Exactly two sheathed worn swords each; no duplicate brush or readable red warning.

rows.narration: Your concern is therefore less cinematic and more constant. How do you remain useful, respectable, and secure while meeting obligations that sometimes pull in different directions?
rows.action: Kenji resumes a straight formal duty posture at the gate threshold, ONE folded order tucked against the obi, slight tired brows but composed expression. Same gate geometry, cabinet and covered bench. Two worn sheathed swords at anatomical-left hip; no stage, armor or battlefield.

rows.narration: You can be proud of the position and exhausted by it at the same time. Those feelings are not contradictory. They are practically the household's most reliable supplies.
rows.action: Kenji and Hana share a quiet weary smile across the familiar low desk after reviewing the household accounts. ONE plain tea cup sits on the desk beside the ledger and small BROWN pouch; no feast or sudden wealth. Keep clothing, hair, modest room and warm daylight.

rows.narration: None of this means a samurai's life was universally worse than everybody else's. Your status brings advantages, and many people around you face heavy burdens without those privileges.
rows.action: At the fixed LEFT rice counter, Kenji stands with modest formal bearing as Merchant weighs out ONE wooden rice measure for him; a few small copper coins lie on the counter. Same olive merchant and indigo Kenji, noren, sacks and parked right cart. Outdoor white tabi with plain straw sandals.

rows.narration: Farmers, servants, laborers, and merchants each inhabit their own complicated worlds. Comparing suffering by costume is a poor way to understand the society they share.
rows.action: Merchant alone refills ONE wooden rice measure from ONE nearby straw sack behind the fixed left counter, illustrating his ordinary labor. Preserve all other rice stock, indigo noren and wooden handcart. No new vendor, swords, changed storefront or readable advertising.

rows.narration: The point is that the familiar picture leaves out the ordinary machinery. Rank needs institutions. Service needs households. A sword needs someone willing and able to maintain it.
rows.action: Kenji and Senior inspect the fitting of ONE sword that REMAINS SHEATHED and WORN at Kenji's left hip. Senior uses ONE EMPTY pointing hand toward the already-worn hilt; he holds NO weapon. EXACTLY FOUR STEEL SWORDS TOTAL: TWO WORN by Kenji and TWO WORN by Senior, black scabbards at each anatomical-left hip. EXACTLY TWO WOODEN practice rods remain mounted on the rear-right wall. No fifth sword, third hilt, loose scabbard, practice prop in hand or drawn blade. Stable hall.

rows.narration: There can be security, education, pride, affection, and opportunity. There can also be debt, supervision, uncertainty, and the pressure to meet expectations you did not choose.
rows.action: Kenji and Hana sit together beside the tidy ledger, ONE plain tea cup and the small BROWN cloth coin pouch, with subtle affectionate smiles. Quiet cooperation within limited resources, same modest HOME and muted costumes; no lavish meal or duplicated pouch.

rows.narration: The merchant closes his books. The superior prepares another instruction. At home, your wife has already worked out which expense must wait until the next payment.
rows.action: Hana alone studies the open household ledger at the fixed low desk and draws ONE copper coin toward the small BROWN pouch, working out which expense must wait. Plain tea cup stays beside the ledger. Same mauve robe, low black bun and HOME geometry; no unrelated shop insert or modern calculator.

rows.narration: Tomorrow you will dress carefully, check the equipment, and go where duty sends you. Your sword will come along, even if the most important object is another written order.
rows.action: Kenji stands at the domain gate ready for another assignment, holding ONE folded cream written order in front of his obi, checking it before stepping through the threshold. Exactly two worn black scabbards at anatomical-left hip. Same late-spring daylight, cabinet and bench, outdoor tabi with straw sandals.

rows.narration: That is why being a samurai could be worse than the picture suggests. Not because every day was a battle, but because the obligations continued when the battles stopped.
rows.action: Kenji passes through the same gate with a composed but tired expression, ONE folded cream order in hand, both sheathed swords still worn. No battle, armor, crowd or altered weather; duty continues in the same ordinary peaceful setting.

rows.narration: You keep the name, the swords, and the place in society. You also keep the bills, the hierarchy, the family worries, and the long list of things requiring your attention.
rows.action: Return to the same modest HOME: Kenji and Hana sit facing the still-open household ledger and small BROWN pouch, illustrating the continuing bills and family concerns. ONE duty letter on desk, both faces thoughtful. Keep room furniture and hair/costumes, no closing luxury party.

rows.narration: This is Samurai Chapters: the lives behind the armor. If you want to step into another life in samurai Japan, there is always another chapter to uncover.
rows.action: Final wide same-master view: Kenji pauses just inside the familiar gate threshold, calm and resolved, ONE folded duty order tucked at obi, two sword scabbards at anatomical-left hip. Gate, covered bench, cabinet and pine remain stable in warm daylight. Clean natural concluding composition, no visible title, subscribe text, logos, invented castle or new costume.
